says: Color therapy on its own, meaning changing the colors used in the home or zones, sets right about half of the Vastu cases, by his estimate. It is the cheapest first-level fix.
ambiguity: '50 पर' is read as 50 percent; the number could be a caption error. 'ठीक हो जाते है' refers to cases or problems getting corrected, not to illness.
classical_check: Silent: color therapy is a modern add-on to Vastu, not a classical remedy with a stated success rate.

hindi: तो ठीक है पित्रों का स्पेसिफिक नहीं है वो जनरिक है
says: He treats the ancestors' (pitru) Vastu placement as a generic remedy, not one tailored to the individual: it is a standard fix that does not need a person-specific study.
ambiguity: 'पित्रों का' leaves the noun out; it could mean the pitru remedy, pitru zone or pitru dosha. I read it as the placement remedy because the next sentence is about where to place them.
classical_check: Differs in spirit: classical Jyotish ties pitru dosha to specific chart factors (Sun, 9th house and the like), so it is chart-specific there.

hindi: डव में लगाओ पितरों को ठीक है
says: Place the ancestors (their pictures or shrine) in the zone he calls 'डव' and that is fine. 'डव' is most likely the Devanagari spelling of the letter W, which is West, because he writes the West the same way a few lines later.
ambiguity: 'डव' could be W (West) or a garbled direction word; the next sentences compare it with the West as if it were different, which clouds the reading.
classical_check: If it is West, this differs from the usual Vastu rule that places the ancestors in the South or South-West (Yama and Pitra side); West is Varuna's belt.

hindi: पितरों का जैसे अब नॉर्थ में लगाना है फोटोग्राफ पितरों की कृपा लेना वो यहां से कहानी है
says: If someone wants to hang the ancestors' photograph in the North in order to draw the ancestors' grace, he calls that a separate story, a different case with its own logic and not the generic placement.
ambiguity: 'वो यहां से कहानी है' is read as 'that is another story'; it could also mean 'the story starts from here'.
classical_check: Differs: classical Vastu keeps ancestor pictures out of the North (the Kubera or Soma side) and puts them toward the South; he is describing a practice, not endorsing it.

hindi: वेस्ट में लगाना है वो अलग है स्थान तो इनका वही है
says: Putting the ancestors in the West is again a different matter, but the ancestors' own place stays the same in either case; only the purpose of hanging the picture changes, not their seat.
ambiguity: 'स्थान तो इनका वही है' may mean the ancestors' fixed place or the place being the same as just mentioned; both readings give the same sense (their seat is fixed).
classical_check: Silent on a split between place and purpose; the classical texts only give each deity one seat.

hindi: हम तो कामकाज का मुद्दा बनाना तो नॉर्थ में लगवा हैं
says: If the aim is made a work or career matter, he would have the ancestors' photo put in the North, so North is treated as the work and career side in his zone scheme.
ambiguity: 'लगवा हैं' is garbled (probably 'लगवाते हैं'). Whether he would really place ancestors in the North, or is describing what others do, is unclear. He gives no house number for the North.
classical_check: Partly agrees: Mahavastu-style zone schemes call the North the career zone, but classical Jyotish ties career to the 10th house, which is the South in the direction-house mapping.

hindi: पितरों की कृपा है वेस्ट में तो स्थान है ही डव में फिर वेस्ट में क्यों लगाना है
says: Raises an objection: if the ancestors' grace is thought to sit in the West and their place is already in 'डव', why would anyone need to put them in the West at all? The point is that grace follows the fixed seat, not where you hang a picture.
ambiguity: Heavily garbled: 'डव' and 'वेस्ट' appear in one sentence as if they were two places, so either 'डव' is not West or the sentence is mis-captioned. The question could also be rhetorical, posed to the audience.
classical_check: Silent: classical Vastu does not discuss this objection.

hindi: पितरों को ही अपना देवता बना दिया भगवान की पूजा से फायदा नहीं हो रहा पितरों से होगा
says: Describes a pattern where people make the ancestors their main deity because worshipping God has given no benefit, hoping the ancestors will deliver instead. He presents this as a particular kind of case, not a general rule.
ambiguity: It is unclear whether he approves of this practice or only reports it; the next sentence calls these 'specific cases'.
classical_check: Silent on replacing the ishta deity with ancestors; classical texts do prescribe pitru worship but alongside, not instead of, deity worship.

hindi: यह फिर स्पेसिफिक केसेस है तो वो स्थान तो एक फिक्स ही होता है उनका
says: Such ancestor-as-deity setups are specific cases, and even then the ancestors' own place is a single fixed zone that does not move with the person's wish.
ambiguity: 'वो स्थान' could mean the ancestors' zone or the deity's zone; the contrast with the deity in the next sentence suggests the ancestors' zone.
classical_check: Agrees in general: the Vastu mandala gives each deity one fixed seat, though which seat holds the pitru is debated.

gist: 'पर देवता की सर ड फड फ होती है ना व देवता' is garbled; the key word after 'देवता की' is lost. It seems to say the deity (occupant) varies while the place is fixed, and it is completed in the next chunk.

hindi: का स्थान नहीं है वो उसका स्थान है जो आपका इष्ट है जो आपका कृपालु कृपा देने वाला वरुण
says: A zone is not owned by one fixed named god; it belongs to whichever deity is your chosen deity (ishta), the one who actually gives you grace, and in the West that seat is called Varuna.
ambiguity: The opening 'का स्थान नहीं है' continues the cut sentence from the previous chunk. Varuna = Neptune comes from his 12-planet scheme, not from this sentence.
classical_check: Differs: Vastu texts fix Varuna as the lord of the West, while here the seat is said to go to whoever gives you grace.

hindi: वरुण क्या है यह भी समझो कंफ्यूजन है
says: Asks what 'Varuna' really is and warns that there is confusion about it. The explanation that follows treats Varuna as an office or seat rather than a single named person.
ambiguity: This is a lead-in; the actual definition comes in the next two sentences.
classical_check: Silent: classical texts treat Varuna as a named deity, so defining him as a seat is his own teaching.

hindi: जैसे प्रधानमंत्री का पद है लाल बहादुर शास्त्री प्रधानमंत्री है मोदी भी प्रधानमंत्री तो प्रधानमंत्री की कुर्सी पर कौन बैठा है वो प्रधानमंत्री है
says: Office-versus-holder analogy: 'Prime Minister' is a post. Lal Bahadur Shastri was PM and so is Modi, so whoever sits in the chair is the PM. A deity's name attached to a direction works the same way: the name belongs to the seat, not to one individual.
ambiguity: The comparison with Vastu zones is made in the next sentence; here it is only the analogy.
classical_check: Silent: it is a teaching analogy, not a classical statement.

hindi: ऐसे डब् फ में वरुण के स्थान पे कौन बैठा है वो वरुण है ये कहानी है
says: Applying the analogy: in the West zone ('W'), whoever is seated at Varuna's place is Varuna. The West seat is defined by position, and its occupant takes the name, whatever god it may be.
ambiguity: 'डब् फ' is read as the letter W for West, backed by the Tirupati example after it. 'ये कहानी है' is read as 'this is the story'.
classical_check: Differs: classical Vastu names Varuna as the lord of the West by identity, not by whoever sits there.

hindi: हो सकता है गणेश गणेश जी हो हो सकता है राम है कृष्ण है कौन है कोई पता नहीं वो स्थान है उसमें बैठ के पूजा पाठ नहीं करना
says: The occupant of the West seat could be Ganesh, Ram, Krishna or anyone, and nobody can know which. What matters is that it is a place, and he says not to sit inside that zone to do puja or recitation.
ambiguity: 'उसमें बैठ के पूजा पाठ नहीं करना' could mean do not do puja while sitting in that zone, or do not worship while sitting in the deity's role. Whether the West or the home's puja seat is meant is not clear.
classical_check: Differs: classical Vastu allows puja while sitting in the West and facing East; the Ishan (North-East) corner is preferred for the puja room.

hindi: जैसे हमारे देवी देवता हैं हमारे कौन से मंदिर है तिरुपति बालाजी वो वेस्ट में देवता लगे हुए हैं बालाजी की जो प्रतिमा है
says: Temple example: in temples such as Tirupati Balaji the deity's idol is installed on the West side of the sanctum. He uses it to show the West is a deity's seat and the idol there is the one who takes that seat.
ambiguity: The sentence is cut off after 'प्रतिमा है'; the point (West placement of the idol) is taken from the next sentences.
classical_check: Agrees: temple sanctums usually place the idol toward the West of the garbhagriha so that it faces East.

hindi: तो वहां ये मुद्दा थोड़ी है उनकी पूजा करनी है क्या पूजा उनकी आरती उतारते हैं व कुछ भी नहीं होता वो स्थान है
says: In the temple example the issue is not whom to worship or whose aarti to perform. He plays down ritual toward the occupant: the real power lies in the place itself, and the ritual alone does little.
ambiguity: 'व कुछ भी नहीं होता' is garbled; it may mean the ritual does nothing by itself or that nothing special happens at that spot.
classical_check: Differs: classical and temple traditions give ritual (puja and aarti) the central role in invoking the deity, not the location alone.

hindi: वो चार्जड प्लेस है चार्जड है ऑलरेडी चार्जड है वेस्ट में जो बैठा है वही भगवान है
says: The West seat is an already-charged place, so whoever is seated in the West is, for that purpose, 'the God'. The zone gives divinity to its occupant instead of the occupant giving it to the zone.
ambiguity: 'चार्जड' (charged) is not defined, so whether it means a power spot, an energy field or a sacred seat is open.
classical_check: Silent: classical Vastu gives each pada of the mandala a presiding deity but has no 'pre-charged place' idea.

hindi: वेस्ट में क्या रख दिया आपने यह कारक वेस्ट में आपने असुर का स्थान होता है इसके साथ असुर रख दिए तो असुरी बन जाएंगे आपके देवता फिर आप असुरी कार्य करोगे
says: Warns that what you put in the West matters: the West also holds the asura (demonic) seat, so if demon-natured things are placed there, your deities turn demonic and you then do demonic deeds. A wrong occupant in the West corrupts conduct.
ambiguity: 'यह कारक' is garbled, and what exactly was placed is not clear (images, objects or a karaka). The 'asur' placement could also be read as being placed next to the asura's seat.
classical_check: Partly agrees: the Vastu mandala has Asura as a deity in the West belt next to Varuna. The claim that wrong placement makes one act demonically is tradition, not classical text.

hindi: उस प्रकार है किसको प्रधानमंत्री बनाओ डिपेंड करता
says: Closes the Prime Minister analogy: the result depends on whom you install in the seat, so the outcome of the West zone depends on the occupant you choose.
ambiguity: The sentence ends in the next chunk with 'है'. 'उस प्रकार' could mean 'in that way' or 'of that kind'.
classical_check: Silent: classical Vastu gives no choice of occupant, so this is his own point.

gist: Closing of the class: 'okay, it is done', thanks, and he ends the day's class.
Announcement for the next class: a small round on combinations of signs (rashi) and planets' houses (bhava), no rule given yet.
Thanks to everyone for joining and for their grace, then pranam and a farewell greeting.
'बहुत सुंदर लव य ल य बत ब ठीक कौन सा ब' is garbled chatter after the class ended.
Chat with someone about a nosebleed (naksir) being due to body heat and what hot food is being fed. Not astrology, and a health remark so nothing is recorded.
Continues the nosebleed chat: says it is no danger, just heat, and to check with a doctor. A health remark, not recorded as a claim.
Tells visitors to take an appointment, phone or ring the bell and come over; offers to get a kundli made or seen, tomorrow or the day after, whenever they like.
Banter about a couple: the husband's 'भजन' (probably weight) is falling while the wife's is rising, a 'two-sided death', so how will life go. A joke.
Tells the noisy people to speak softly and keep quiet, with a 'my God' exclamation.
'शनि एक्टिवेट होना चाहिए कैसे हो रहा है मेरे सेरेने मैं करूं क्या' appears inside the jokes. Saturn 'should be activated' is a one-line aside whose context is lost, so no rule is recorded.
Pun on 'khan': 'am I a mine (khan) of vices?', many Khans lead the film industry, so we too will become a 'khan of vices'.
Banter: 'it is nothing, the man is turning into a boy; it is your party, enjoy'.
Joke to the ladies: keep your husband trapped; the ladies' problem is that the husband is not stuck with them; 'this is a blessing, a great virtue'.
Talk with someone nearby, perhaps a child: 'walking about like a teddy bear', 'keep it, son, take it, son, we will talk'; the video ends with music.
A last 'yes, okay' to someone off-camera.
